facts.text: I have severe pain in my right groin.
The pain in my knees and my groin started immediately after the accident.
I was in a car crash: a rear-end collision, and I was driving the car at the back.
My right leg looks slightly shorter than the other one, and it's bent, pulled in toward the other leg and turned inward.
I don't have any belly pain.
I don't have any chest pain.
I don't have any significant medical problems.
I work as an elementary school teacher.

findings.name: hip examination
aliases: range of motion of the legs
findings.result: Inspection: right leg slightly shortened, flexed, adducted and internally rotated; no visible wounds. Palpation: right groin tender. Range of motion: right leg limited by pain and abnormal positioning; left leg normal.

findings.name: pelvic X-ray
findings.result: No fracture of the pelvic ring or femoral neck; alignment suggests posterior dislocation of the right hip.

aliases: posterior dislocation of the right hip

quotes.f003: immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident
quotes.f004: involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car
quotes.f006: Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated
quotes.f011: Works as an elementary school teacher

f006: The leg posture is listed as a secondary symptom and repeated in the exam inspection (x005). Kept as a patient fact because a patient can see and feel how her own leg lies; worded in lay terms.

x005.source_text: The right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated. No visible wounds. + Tender to palpation + Limited due to pain and abnormal positioning + Normal range of motion

x007.source_text: No fractures identified in the pelvic ring or femoral neck, but alignment suggests posterior dislocation of the right hip.

leakage.reason: The pelvic X-ray result names the diagnosis (posterior dislocation of the right hip). This is the test's answer; the finding name does not reveal it.

source_issues: The Review_of_Systems starts with 'Alert and active.', an observer description rather than a patient-reported symptom.
notes: The immediate onset after the crash applies to both the groin and the knee pain, so it is a standalone fact (f003). The crash is a symptom-context fact (f004) with the seatbelt as its child.
The musculoskeletal leaves are split by region as a doctor would request them: hip/leg (inspection, right-groin palpation, range of motion of both legs) and knees (tenderness over both kneecaps).
'Alert and active.' (ROS) is observer-only and the exam has no mental-status leaf, so it goes to qc.extras.acting_notes.

extras.objective_for_doctor: Conduct a thorough assessment of a patient presenting with right groin pain and abnormal leg positioning following a rear-end collision, and diagnose appropriately.
